operation_tail.detail: The current official ONSPD release used for lifecycle and schema controls is May 2026; older February 2026 content is retained only as historical methodology evidence.
The May 2026 ONSPD dataset is recorded with its official 10 June 2026 catalogue update date.
ONSPD and NSPL releases follow the documented February, May, August and November quarterly cycle.
The May 2026 full ONSPD download is catalogued at 235 MB; this package size is not confused with hosted-table storage or Ofcom archive size.
The full ONSPD package contains multiple CSV files divided so postcode areas can be opened separately; area partitioning is preserved during ingestion.
The May 2026 directory explicitly covers both current and terminated UK postcodes.
The release links postcodes to current statutory administrative, electoral, health and other area geographies.
Legacy pre-2002 health-area fields remain historical geography attributes and are not treated as current health boundaries.
England and Wales 1991 Census enumeration-district links are retained as vintage-specific historical fields.
England and Wales 2001 Output Area and Super Output Area codes remain distinct from later census geographies.
Northern Ireland 2001 Output Area and Super Output Area fields are kept in their own national vintage.
Scotland 2001 Output Area and Data Zone fields are not mixed with England, Wales or Northern Ireland SOA fields.
The May 2026 release contains 2021 Census Output Area and Super Output Area geographies for England, Wales and Northern Ireland.
Scotland uses 2022 Census Output Areas, Data Zones and Intermediate Zones, separate from the 2021 census vintages elsewhere.
The May 2026 release was updated on 4 June 2026 to correct corrupted SSR95CD values for some postcodes.
Any May 2026 cache or hosted extract must be bound to the corrected release rather than an earlier same-month artifact.
Royal Mail, Gridlink, LPS Northern Ireland, Ordnance Survey and ONS intellectual-property notices are retained with the source record.
ONSPD supports area-based statistics from postcoded data; this purpose does not make a postcode centroid an exact parcel boundary.
The publisher is recorded as ONS Geography within the Office for National Statistics rather than an unaffiliated mirror.
The May 2026 hosted ONSPD table is an official API-accessible representation separate from the downloadable multi-CSV package.
Hosted-table exports and the ArcGIS GeoService are treated as representations of one release, not independent corroborating sources.
The hosted table is catalogued at 2.31 GB and must not be compared directly with the compressed 235 MB full-package size.
The official hosted-table service advertises a maximum record count of 1,000, so complete extraction requires deterministic pagination.
The hosted service uses standardized queries; filter expressions are validated rather than relying on provider-specific SQL behavior.
The May 2026 hosted ONSPD object is a table without geometry properties; coordinate columns must be parsed as attributes.
ArcGIS ObjectId is system-maintained pagination metadata and is not substituted for postcode identity.
The hosted schema exposes pcd7, pcd8 and pcds postcode representations; normalization preserves the source forms for audit.
The dointr field is retained as the postcode introduction date rather than inferred from first local observation.
The doterm field is the explicit termination-date attribute and remains blank for postcodes without a recorded termination.
cty25cd is treated as a 2025 county-code field; the year suffix is part of the schema contract.
ced25cd remains a 2025 county electoral-division code and is not merged with ward codes.
lad25cd is retained as the 2025 local-authority district code used by the May 2026 release.
wd25cd is validated independently from county electoral divisions and other administrative code families.
parncp25cd is retained as the 2025 parish or non-civil-parished-area code.
The hosted table's usrtypind header is mapped explicitly to the documented small-user or large-user indicator.
east1m, north1m and gridind are parsed as a coordinated positional-quality group rather than isolated values.
hlth19cd and nhser24cd carry different health-geography vintages and are not collapsed into one generic health field.
ctry25cd and rgn25cd are separately validated 2025 country and region code fields.
The corrected ssr95cd field is present in the official May 2026 hosted schema and remains subject to corrected-release binding.
pcon24cd is treated as the 2024 Westminster constituency code rather than a timeless constituency identifier.
itl25cd retains its 2025 International Territorial Level vintage and is not renamed to an older NUTS field.
oa01cd, lsoa01cd and msoa01cd are retained as a coherent 2001 hierarchy.
oa11cd, lsoa11cd and msoa11cd are retained as a coherent 2011 hierarchy distinct from 2001 and 2021 fields.
wz11cd is treated as a workplace-zone geography and is not substituted for residential Output Areas.
npark16cd is retained as a distinct national-park code whose allocation rules can differ from ordinary best-fit geographies.
The hosted table exposes lat and long as attributes; they remain derived coordinate representations rather than independent parcel surveys.
The current hosted schema confirms separate oa21cd, lsoa21cd and msoa21cd fields.
ruc21ind is retained as a 2021 rural-urban classification indicator, not inferred from coordinate density.
Year suffixes such as 24, 25 and 26 are preserved because they identify the geography vintage used by each column.
Most hosted ONSPD attributes are exposed as strings; dates, numeric coordinates and indicators require validated conversions.
Hosted fields are generally nullable, so blanks remain unavailable values unless an official rule supplies them.
The current NSPL release is May 2026 and remains a separate product from ONSPD.
NSPL allocates higher geographies by best fit from 2021 Output Areas, while national parks and Workplace Zones use exact-fit allocation.
Postcode products derived from Code-Point Open require OGL attribution plus OS, Royal Mail and ONS notices; commercial BT data requires separate LPS licensing.

Fifty-five current-release, hosted-schema, lifecycle, geography, methodology and licensing controls were published line by line; exact Ofcom coverage candidates remain blocked until strict r2 byte validation.
